candidate.blueprint_locator: Appendix A, Management of Care — Performance Improvement, printed p.22.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — quality improvement of transfer processes
candidate.educational_objective: Respond to recurring care-process failures through reporting, structured quality-improvement review, evidence-based change and outcome evaluation.

options.A: Report the recurring care issue through the appropriate process and participate in a structured review of causes, evidence-based changes, and outcome data.
options.B: Identify one nurse involved in the most recent transfer and treat that individual as the sole cause without examining the recurring process problem.
options.C: Ignore the pattern if no client has yet been seriously harmed because performance-improvement review should begin only after a sentinel event occurs.
options.D: Create a personal transfer form and use it without informing the unit because individual undocumented workarounds are preferable to a coordinated improvement process.

candidate.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN Test Plan expects RNs to report identified client-care issues to appropriate personnel, participate in PI/QI processes, use research and references for improvement actions, and evaluate the impact of improvement measures on client care. A applies those activities to a recurring transfer-process problem. B reduces a system pattern to individual blame, C waits for serious harm before acting, and D creates an uncoordinated workaround rather than a structured improvement process.
candidate.source_claim_supported: RNs should report recurring care issues and participate in structured evidence-based quality improvement with outcome evaluation.
candidate.source_locator: Appendix A, Management of Care, Performance Improvement, printed p.22: participate in PI/QI processes; report identified care issues; use research/references; evaluate impact on client care.
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: A staff nurse notices repeated omissions in medication-reconciliation information during transfers between units. Which response best supports quality improvement?
